mechanism: Both drugs have anticholinergic properties and CNS effects; bupropion is metabolized by CYP3A4/2D6 and oxybutynin is a CYP3A4 substrate, creating potential for increased levels and additive anticholinergic toxicity.
action: Monitor for anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, cognitive effects); consider alternative antimuscarinergic agent or dose adjustment; assess seizure risk as both drugs lower seizure threshold.
